target.workload: cache-off c32, 8192 input tokens, 1024 output tokens, complete within 300 seconds

venue.host_contract: 48 vCPU, 180 GiB instance memory, one full GPU; custom image or container launch is supported
venue.orderability_evidence: G4 is documented GA/current in Compute Engine; exact shape and zone are public. Actual quota/capacity remains account-specific and was not queried.
venue.container_contract: Compute Engine supports custom images and create-with-container with --container-privileged; GPU driver installation is documented for G4/CUDA 13.1+. The unchanged published vLLM container can therefore be supplied without provider mutation in this gate.
venue.billing_minimum: not separately bound in this zero-cost gate; Compute Engine public pricing and per-second billing are documented
venue.storage_network_inclusions: not included in the GPU/VM rate; disk, image, networking, and egress are separate charges

rate.basis: public on-demand whole-instance rate, not experimental metered rate
rate.rate_scope_note: The displayed G4 Standard on-demand price is for the one-GPU g4-standard-48 VM; disk, image, networking, and egress remain excluded, so this is a lower bound on all-in cost.

economic_gate.venue_rate_only_usd_per_million_note: At the generous measured-envelope cap below; actual performance and all non-VM costs are unknown.

physical_envelope.evidence_class: derived conservative bound, not transferred throughput
physical_envelope.bound_method: Start with measured L40S c16 throughput; apply the smaller SM or bandwidth scale factor (min(188/142, 1597/864)=1.32394), then multiply by 2.0 to allow a very generous c32/Blackwell/runtime benefit.
physical_envelope.interpretation: Even the 2x envelope is 41.7% below the 2431.869 tok/s requirement; this is an economic close, not a claim that SM120 cannot run the model.

sources.title: Google Cloud accelerator-optimized VM pricing
sources.evidence: g4-standard-48 one-GPU on-demand $4.49993/hour; page labels columns and separates disk/network pricing

sources.title: Google Cloud GPU machine types
sources.evidence: G4 is RTX PRO 6000, 96 GB GDDR7 ECC, 1597 GB/s; intended for ML inference

sources.title: Google Cloud GPU locations
sources.evidence: full-GPU G4 shapes are documented and fractional G4 shapes are restricted to us-central1-b

sources.title: Google Cloud create-with-container
sources.evidence: container image, privileged container, accelerator, and host mounts are supported by the public launch contract

uncertainties: Quota and instantaneous capacity were not queried; no account-specific order guarantee is claimed.
The physical envelope is deliberately conservative but analytical; only the L40S reference is measured.
Disk, image, networking, egress, and license charges can only increase the required throughput.
